title: Learning Urban Access Costs from Origin-Destination Flows via Inverse Optimal Transport
abstract: arXiv:2606.14157v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Cities deliver basic services through mixed public-private facility networks, including schools, clinics, transit providers, and subsidized service points. In these systems, planners often observe where households go, but not the latent cost function through which they trade off factors such as distance, price, and institutional access. We study this urban problem through school choice in the Philippines, where the country's largest national education subsidy is intended to redirect learners from congested public schools to participating private schools. Treating school-to-school enrollment flows as an entropic optimal transport plan, we recover latent choice costs using two complementary inverse optimal transport models: an interpretable distance-banded model with a subsidy term, and a neural cost model trained through a differentiable Sinkhorn forward pass. translated_title: 通过逆最优传输从起讫点流量中学习城市可达性成本
translated_abstract: 城市通过公私混合的设施网络提供基本服务，包括学校、诊所、交通服务提供商和补贴服务点。在这些系统中，规划者通常能观察到家庭去向，但无法观察到他们权衡距离、价格和制度可达性等因素的潜在成本函数。我们通过菲律宾的学校选择问题研究这一城市问题，该国最大的国家教育补贴旨在将学习者从拥挤的公立学校引导至参与计划的私立学校。我们将校际入学流量视为熵正则化最优传输计划，并使用两个互补的逆最优传输模型来恢复潜在选择成本：一个是带有补贴项、可解释的距离分带模型，另一个是通过可微分Sinkhorn前向传播训练的神经成本模型。该方法应用于23,820条观测流量中283,016次学习者出行数据……
tldr: 该论文提出两种互补的逆最优传输模型——带补贴项的可解释距离分带模型和基于可微分Sinkhorn前向传播训练的神经成本模型——从菲律宾28万余次学生择校出行流量中恢复潜在选择成本，以揭示家庭在距离、价格与制度可达性之间的权衡机制。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes two complementary inverse optimal transport models—an interpretable distance-banded model with a subsidy term and a neural cost model trained via a differentiable Sinkhorn forward pass—to recover latent school choice costs from over 283,000 learner trips across 23,820 observed flows in the Philippines.
